title: 1 Kings Chapter 19 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Kings chapter 19 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Kings Chapter 19 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Kings Chapter 19.

questions.question: Who told Jezebel all that Elijah had done, including how he had slain all the prophets with the sword?
questions.correctAnswer: Ahab
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:1 states that Ahab told Jezebel all that Elijah had done, including how he had slain all the prophets with the sword.

questions.question: What threat did Jezebel send to Elijah through a messenger?
options: She would make his life as the life of one of the slain prophets by tomorrow
She would send soldiers to capture Elijah
She would exile Elijah from the land
questions.correctAnswer: She would make his life as the life of one of the slain prophets by tomorrow
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:2 records Jezebel's threat that she would make Elijah's life like that of one of the slain prophets by tomorrow about this time.

questions.question: Where did Elijah go after he saw Jezebel's threat?
questions.correctAnswer: Beersheba
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:3 shows Elijah arose, fled for his life, and came to Beersheba, which belongs to Judah.

questions.question: True or False: Elijah left his servant in Beersheba when he went a day's journey into the wilderness.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:3 states Elijah left his servant at Beersheba before going a day's journey into the wilderness.

questions.question: Under which kind of tree did Elijah sit down and request that the LORD take away his life?
questions.correctAnswer: Juniper tree
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:4 records Elijah went under a juniper tree and requested the LORD to take away his life.

questions.question: What did Elijah say to the LORD when he requested to die?
options: It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life
questions.correctAnswer: It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:4 records Elijah saying, 'It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life; for I am not better than my fathers.'

questions.question: Who touched Elijah while he lay sleeping under the juniper tree?
questions.correctAnswer: An angel
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:5 states that an angel touched Elijah and told him to arise and eat.

questions.question: True or False: When Elijah looked, he saw a cake baked on the coals and a cruse of water at his head.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:6 describes Elijah seeing a cake baked on coals and a cruse of water at his head.

questions.question: After eating and drinking, what did Elijah do according to 1 Kings 19:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Laid down again
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:6 says Elijah ate and drank, then laid down again.

questions.question: What reason did the angel give Elijah for telling him to arise and eat the second time?
options: Because the journey is too great for thee
questions.correctAnswer: Because the journey is too great for thee
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:7 states the angel told Elijah to arise and eat because the journey is too great for him.

questions.question: True or False: Elijah traveled in the strength of the food and drink for twenty days and nights to Mount Horeb.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:8 says Elijah traveled for forty days and forty nights to Horeb, not twenty.

questions.question: In 1 Kings 19, which event comes first?
options: The angel touches Elijah and tells him to eat
Jezebel sends a messenger to threaten Elijah
Elijah casts his mantle upon Elisha
questions.correctAnswer: Jezebel sends a messenger to threaten Elijah
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:2 records Jezebel sending a messenger to Elijah before the angel touches Elijah (v.5), Elijah's arrival at Horeb (v.9), or casting his mantle on Elisha (v.19).

questions.question: What did Elijah do with his servant when he fled to Beersheba?
questions.correctAnswer: Left him there
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:3 says Elijah left his servant in Beersheba when he fled for his life.

questions.question: True or False: Elijah requested for himself that he might die because he felt he was better than his fathers.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:4 shows Elijah said, 'for I am not better than my fathers,' expressing humility, not superiority.

questions.question: What kind of food did the angel provide for Elijah under the juniper tree?
questions.correctAnswer: A cake baked on coals
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:6 states that Elijah saw a cake baked on coals provided by the angel.

medium.title: 1 Kings Chapter 19 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Kings Chapter 19 to real-life situations.

questions.question: How long did Elijah travel in the strength of the food given to him before reaching Mount Horeb?
questions.correctAnswer: Forty days and forty nights
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:8 states that Elijah went in the strength of the food for forty days and forty nights unto Horeb the mount of God. This highlights God's provision sustaining Elijah for an extended journey.

questions.question: What question does the LORD ask Elijah when He speaks to him at the cave in Horeb?
options: Where will you go now, Elijah?
questions.correctAnswer: What doest thou here, Elijah?
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 19:9, the LORD asks Elijah, 'What doest thou here, Elijah?' when Elijah is in the cave. This question invites Elijah to reflect on his circumstances and purpose.

questions.question: According to Elijah’s reply to God, why does Elijah say he is alone?
options: Because the children of Israel have forsaken God's covenant, thrown down altars, and slain prophets
Because he was exiled from the kingdom
Because he lost faith in God
questions.correctAnswer: Because the children of Israel have forsaken God's covenant, thrown down altars, and slain prophets
questions.explanation: Elijah explains in 1 Kings 19:10 that he is very jealous for the LORD God of hosts because the children of Israel have forsaken God's covenant, thrown down His altars, and slain His prophets, leaving Elijah as the only one left.

questions.question: What natural phenomena did the LORD use to pass by Elijah on the mount, and in which was He not found?
options: A great wind, an earthquake, and a fire
A thunderstorm, a flood, and fire
A strong wind, lightning, and an earthquake
A fire, an earthquake, and a great flood
questions.correctAnswer: A great wind, an earthquake, and a fire
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:11-12 describes a great and strong wind, an earthquake, and a fire passing by Elijah, but the LORD was not in any of these; rather, He was in a still small voice following them.

questions.question: What followed the fire in which the LORD was not found, according to 1 Kings 19?
questions.correctAnswer: A still small voice
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:12 states that after the fire, the LORD was found in a still small voice. This teaches that God's presence is not always in dramatic displays but can be in quietness and subtlety.

questions.question: How does Elijah respond when he hears the still small voice of the LORD?
options: He wraps his face in his mantle and stands at the cave’s entrance
questions.correctAnswer: He wraps his face in his mantle and stands at the cave’s entrance
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 19:13, Elijah wrapped his face in his mantle and went out to stand at the entrance of the cave when he heard the voice of the LORD. This shows reverence and readiness to listen.

questions.question: What does the LORD instruct Elijah to do after his encounter at Mount Horeb?
options: Return on his way to the wilderness of Damascus and anoint new leaders
Go to Ahab and Jezebel to confront them
Travel to Jerusalem to seek counsel
questions.correctAnswer: Return on his way to the wilderness of Damascus and anoint new leaders
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:15 commands Elijah to return on his way to the wilderness of Damascus and anoint Hazael, Jehu, and Elisha to their respective roles, demonstrating obedience and God’s plan for leadership.

questions.question: What is the significance of Elijah anointing Hazael, Jehu, and Elisha as described in 1 Kings 19?
options: They will all become kings of Israel
They will each lead Israel in different regions and roles to fulfill God's judgment
They will build altars to Baal
They will become prophets to challenge Elijah
questions.correctAnswer: They will each lead Israel in different regions and roles to fulfill God's judgment
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:15-17 explains that Hazael will be king over Syria, Jehu king over Israel, and Elisha prophet in Elijah's place; their roles will accomplish God's justice as part of His plan.

questions.question: What promise does God give regarding those who have not bowed to Baal or kissed him?
options: They will be left in Israel as a faithful remnant
They will be punished for their disobedience
They will be exiled to another land
questions.correctAnswer: They will be left in Israel as a faithful remnant
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:18 reveals God has left 7,000 people in Israel who have not bowed to Baal or kissed him, illustrating God's mercy and the existence of a faithful remnant.

questions.question: What action did Elijah take when he found Elisha plowing with twelve yoke of oxen?
options: He ignored Elisha and continued on his way
He threw his mantle upon Elisha
He asked Elisha to pray for him
He challenged Elisha to a contest
questions.correctAnswer: He threw his mantle upon Elisha
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 19:19, Elijah passed by Elisha and cast his mantle upon him, symbolizing the calling of Elisha to succeed Elijah as prophet.

questions.question: What did Elisha request before following Elijah, and what was Elijah’s response?
options: To visit his family; Elijah said go back
To finish plowing; Elijah said wait
To kiss his father and mother; Elijah said go back again
To gather his belongings; Elijah said take them now
questions.correctAnswer: To kiss his father and mother; Elijah said go back again
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:20 shows Elisha asked to kiss his parents before following Elijah, but Elijah told him to go back again, testing Elisha’s commitment before full discipleship.

questions.question: How did Elisha demonstrate his commitment to following Elijah after the initial request?
options: He returned to plow his field
He slaughtered a yoke of oxen, boiled their flesh, and gave it to the people to eat
He built an altar to the LORD
He wrote a letter to the king
questions.correctAnswer: He slaughtered a yoke of oxen, boiled their flesh, and gave it to the people to eat
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:21 tells that after returning from his parents, Elisha slaughtered oxen and fed the people, signifying a definitive break from his past life to fully follow Elijah.

questions.question: True or False: Elijah’s journey to Mount Horeb was sustained by an angel providing him food and water.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:5-7 shows an angel touched Elijah and provided food and water to sustain him for his journey to Mount Horeb, demonstrating God's care.

questions.question: True or False: Elijah was confident and felt that many prophets remained faithful in Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Elijah expressed in 1 Kings 19:10 and 19:14 that he felt alone and believed he was the only one left faithful, showing his discouragement and isolation.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD’s presence is always revealed through powerful natural events like wind, earthquake, or fire.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:11-12 explains that the LORD was not in the wind, earthquake, or fire, but in a still small voice, teaching that God’s presence can be subtle and quiet.

hard.title: 1 Kings Chapter 19 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Kings Chapter 19.

questions.question: Who did the LORD instruct Elijah to anoint as king over Syria?
questions.correctAnswer: Hazael
questions.explanation: The LORD specifically told Elijah to anoint Hazael to be king over Syria, as stated in 1 Kings 19:15.

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 19, who was Elijah commanded to anoint as king over Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Jehu the son of Nimshi
questions.explanation: Elijah was instructed to anoint Jehu the son of Nimshi as king over Israel, as stated in 1 Kings 19:16.

questions.question: Who was Elijah told to anoint to be prophet in his place?
questions.correctAnswer: Elisha the son of Shaphat
questions.explanation: The LORD told Elijah to anoint Elisha the son of Shaphat of Abelmeholah to be prophet in his room, as found in 1 Kings 19:16.

questions.question: What will happen to those who escape the sword of Hazael according to Elijah's prophecy?
questions.correctAnswer: Jehu will slay them
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:17 says that him who escapes the sword of Hazael shall be slain by Jehu.

questions.question: What does Elijah say about how many faithful remain in Israel who have not bowed to Baal?
questions.correctAnswer: Seven thousand
questions.explanation: Elijah states that the LORD has left seven thousand in Israel who have not bowed to Baal, in 1 Kings 19:18.

questions.question: What was Elisha doing when Elijah found him?
options: Plowing with twelve yoke of oxen
questions.correctAnswer: Plowing with twelve yoke of oxen
questions.explanation: Elisha was found by Elijah plowing with twelve yoke of oxen before him, as described in 1 Kings 19:19.

questions.question: What symbolic act did Elijah perform to call Elisha to follow him?
questions.correctAnswer: Cast his mantle upon him
questions.explanation: Elijah cast his mantle upon Elisha as a symbol of calling him to be his successor, as recorded in 1 Kings 19:19.

questions.question: How did Elisha respond when Elijah told him to follow him immediately?
options: He asked to kiss his parents first
He asked for a sign from God
questions.correctAnswer: He asked to kiss his parents first
questions.explanation: Elisha requested to kiss his father and mother before following Elijah, as described in 1 Kings 19:20.

questions.question: What did Elisha do with the oxen he left behind when he followed Elijah?
options: Slew them, boiled their flesh, and gave to the people
questions.correctAnswer: Slew them, boiled their flesh, and gave to the people
questions.explanation: Elisha killed the oxen, boiled their flesh with the instruments, and gave it to the people to eat, as told in 1 Kings 19:21.

questions.question: True or False: Elijah was told by the LORD to go to the wilderness of Damascus after receiving instructions about anointing kings and a prophet.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:15 states that the LORD told Elijah to return on his way to the wilderness of Damascus after being given his instructions.

questions.question: True or False: Elijah said he was the only prophet left in Israel after the killing of the other prophets.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Elijah said he alone was left, but 1 Kings 19:18 reveals the LORD had preserved seven thousand who had not bowed to Baal, so Elijah was mistaken in thinking he was the only one left.

questions.question: Which literary device is most evident when Elijah experiences wind, earthquake, fire, and then a still small voice on Mount Horeb?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: The sequence of powerful natural phenomena followed by a still small voice forms a chiasm, highlighting the contrast between external displays and God's true presence, as seen in 1 Kings 19:11-12.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of God's presence being revealed in a 'still small voice' similar to 1 Kings 19:12?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 46:10
questions.explanation: Psalm 46:10 states 'Be still, and know that I am God,' which echoes the theme of God's presence in quietness as in 1 Kings 19:12.

questions.question: The word 'mantle' used when Elijah casts it on Elisha in 1 Kings 19:19, in the original Hebrew, symbolizes what?
questions.correctAnswer: A garment representing prophetic authority
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for mantle (מְעִיל, me'il) signifies a cloak representing Elijah's prophetic office, symbolizing the transfer of authority to Elisha, as seen in 1 Kings 19:19.

questions.question: Which New Testament event can be seen as a fulfillment or echo of Elijah’s commissioning of Elisha as a prophet in 1 Kings 19:16-21?
options: The calling of the twelve apostles by Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: The calling of the twelve apostles by Jesus
questions.explanation: Just as Elijah commissions Elisha to continue the prophetic ministry, Jesus calling the twelve apostles in the New Testament continues God's mission through chosen successors, paralleling the commissioning in 1 Kings 19:16-21.

theological.title: 1 Kings Chapter 19 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Kings Chapter 19 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine attribute is especially demonstrated by the LORD's appearance as a "still small voice" after the wind, earthquake, and fire at Mount Horeb?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereignty and subtlety
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:11-12 shows that God was not in the dramatic natural events but came in a "still small voice," demonstrating His sovereign control and subtle, discerning presence rather than merely power displayed through force.

questions.question: According to 1 Kings 19, what theological reason does Elijah give for his despair and request for death under the juniper tree?
options: He believes he is better than his ancestors
He sees himself as the only faithful servant left and fears for his life
He is physically weak and tired
questions.correctAnswer: He sees himself as the only faithful servant left and fears for his life
questions.explanation: Elijah states in 1 Kings 19:10 and 19:4 that he is jealous for God because Israel has forsaken the covenant, killed prophets, and only he remains, fearing for his own life.

questions.question: What does the LORD’s instruction to Elijah to anoint Hazael, Jehu, and Elisha reveal about God’s providence in this chapter?
options: God’s providence is limited to Israel’s kings
God orchestrates the rise and fall of rulers to fulfill His purposes
God leaves political affairs to human discretion
questions.correctAnswer: God orchestrates the rise and fall of rulers to fulfill His purposes
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 19:15-16, God commands Elijah to anoint rulers and a prophet, showing divine providence in establishing leadership according to His redemptive plan.

questions.question: How does Elijah’s journey of forty days and nights to Mount Horeb (1 Kings 19:8) symbolically relate to biblical themes of testing and preparation?
options: It parallels Israel’s 40 years in the wilderness
It represents a punishment from God
It is an arbitrary journey with no symbolic meaning
questions.correctAnswer: It parallels Israel’s 40 years in the wilderness
questions.explanation: The 40-day journey in 1 Kings 19:8 echoes Israel’s 40 years in the wilderness, symbolizing a period of testing, reliance on God, and preparation for new mission.

questions.question: What doctrine about God’s sustaining provision is taught by the angel’s feeding of Elijah with cake and water in the wilderness?
options: God’s provision is limited to material needs
God provides spiritually but not physically
God sustains His servants physically to fulfill their spiritual mission
God expects His servants to provide for themselves
questions.correctAnswer: God sustains His servants physically to fulfill their spiritual mission
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:5-7 shows an angel providing food and water to Elijah, teaching that God cares for the physical needs of His servants to empower their spiritual calling.

questions.question: What theological insight about human limitation and divine strength is conveyed by Elijah eating twice before traveling forty days?
options: Human strength alone is sufficient for God’s work
God’s provision enables endurance beyond natural capacity
Elijah was overconfident in his abilities
Physical nourishment is irrelevant to spiritual tasks
questions.correctAnswer: God’s provision enables endurance beyond natural capacity
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 19:7-8, Elijah eats and drinks before a supernaturally sustained journey, illustrating that divine provision transcends human limitations for mission.

questions.question: What does 1 Kings 19:18 teach about God’s grace and preservation of a faithful remnant within a sinful nation?
options: God preserves a remnant who remain true to Him
God’s grace is limited to the prophets
questions.correctAnswer: God preserves a remnant who remain true to Him
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:18 explicitly states that God has left seven thousand in Israel who have not bowed to Baal, revealing His grace in preserving a faithful remnant.

questions.question: How does Elijah’s casting of his mantle on Elisha (1 Kings 19:19) symbolize the transmission of prophetic authority and continuity of God’s mission?
options: It symbolizes Elijah’s rejection of Elisha
It signifies the passing of prophetic authority and continuation of God’s work
It is a casual gesture without deeper meaning
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies the passing of prophetic authority and continuation of God’s work
questions.explanation: Verse 1 Kings 19:19 shows Elijah casting his mantle on Elisha, symbolizing the transfer of prophetic authority and continuity in God’s redemptive mission.

questions.question: What theological synthesis about God's communication with humans is taught by combining Elijah’s experiences in 1 Kings 19:9 and 1 Kings 19:13?
options: God only speaks through loud and dramatic means
God’s communication requires human readiness and reverence
God’s voice is always accompanied by natural phenomena
God is silent and inaccessible to prophets
questions.correctAnswer: God’s communication requires human readiness and reverence
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 19:9 God asks Elijah why he is there, and in 19:13 Elijah responds reverently after hearing the still small voice, showing that God’s communication requires attentive and humble readiness.

questions.question: What does the narrative arc of Elijah’s fear and God’s reassurance in 1 Kings 19:3-4 and 1 Kings 19:18 reveal about God’s redemptive faithfulness?
options: God abandons His servants in times of fear
God’s faithfulness includes preserving a faithful remnant despite apparent defeat
God’s plan fails when His servants despair
God’s faithfulness depends on human strength
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness includes preserving a faithful remnant despite apparent defeat
questions.explanation: Elijah flees fearing for his life (19:3-4), but God reassures him that 7,000 remain faithful (19:18), showing God’s unwavering redemptive faithfulness.

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 19:14 reveal a theological understanding of covenant faithfulness and its breach by Israel?
options: Israel has faithfully kept the covenant
Israel has forsaken God’s covenant and killed His prophets
Elijah is wrong about Israel’s faithfulness
The covenant is irrelevant to Israel’s history
questions.correctAnswer: Israel has forsaken God’s covenant and killed His prophets
questions.explanation: Elijah laments in 1 Kings 19:14 that Israel has forsaken God’s covenant, destroyed altars, and slain prophets, emphasizing covenant breach and rebellion.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by God’s instruction to Elijah to anoint not only kings but also a prophet (1 Kings 19:15-16)?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s providential governance and calling
questions.explanation: God’s command to anoint rulers and a prophet (1 Kings 19:15-16) reveals His providential governance over political and spiritual realms, orchestrating history and calling servants.

questions.question: What apologetic response does 1 Kings 19:11-13 provide to sceptics who claim that God must always reveal Himself through grand natural displays to be real or powerful?
options: God only reveals Himself through earthquakes and fire
God’s power is shown in subtlety, not just spectacular events
God does not communicate with humans
Natural phenomena are the only proof of God’s existence
questions.correctAnswer: God’s power is shown in subtlety, not just spectacular events
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:11-13 shows God not in dramatic elements but in a still small voice, refuting the sceptic’s claim by demonstrating that divine power and presence often manifest in subtle, intimate ways.

questions.question: How does Elijah’s ministry transition in 1 Kings 19:19-21 reflect the doctrine of succession and continuity in God’s redemptive plan?
options: Elijah’s ministry ends abruptly without a successor
Elijah’s passing of the mantle to Elisha shows intentional continuation of prophetic mission
God abandons His plan after Elijah
questions.correctAnswer: Elijah’s passing of the mantle to Elisha shows intentional continuation of prophetic mission
questions.explanation: The narrative in 1 Kings 19:19-21 reveals Elijah anointing Elisha as his prophetic successor, affirming the doctrine that God ensures the continuity of His work through appointed servants.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching about God’s justice and judgment can be drawn from 1 Kings 19:16-17 and 1 Kings 19:18?
options: God’s judgment is random and unjust
God’s justice involves appointed agents to execute judgment and preservation of a faithful remnant
questions.correctAnswer: God’s justice involves appointed agents to execute judgment and preservation of a faithful remnant
questions.explanation: Verses 1 Kings 19:16-17 describe anointing of kings to carry out judgment, while 19:18 reveals preservation of a faithful remnant, together teaching God’s balanced justice and mercy.
